items.claim: The four-item numeral formula (אַרְבָּ֣עָה, 30:24) is fully itemized across 30:25-28 and bracketed by disclosed single-witness petuchot at 30:23 and 30:28, giving the numerical_saying row a sound seam warrant on both edges.
items.evidence: oshb:Prov.30.24 אַרְבָּ֣עָה opens the count and matches source bytes exactly; the four items (ants 30:25, rock badgers 30:26, locusts 30:27, lizard 30:28) fill exactly four verses; pmarks_Prov.json confirms PE at Prov.30.23 and Prov.30.28 only in this stretch, matching the row's bracket claim; the preceding neighbor unit (30:21-23, a different three/four saying about unbearable things) shares no content token with 30:24, so the opening seam is clean and not cross-seam-cohesive with the prior row.
tier_citations: tier-1 (numeral formula + itemization, oshb text, re-collated)

items.claim: The three/four formula at 30:29 is honestly itemized as an uneven 1-then-3 split across 30:30-31, and the row's closing boundary at 30:31|30:32 is warranted by a genuine register shift (third-person description to second-person imperative) rather than by absent parashah support, which the row correctly does not overclaim as counterevidence.
items.evidence: oshb:Prov.30.29 שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה...וְ֝אַרְבָּעָ֗ה byte-matches the source at word positions 1 and 5; 30:30 names one item (לַ֭יִשׁ), 30:31 packs three (זרזיר/תיש/מלך), an uneven distribution the row discloses in device_notes rather than concealing; pmarks_Prov.json confirms PE only at Prov.30.28 in this stretch, none at Prov.30.31, so the row correctly rests its closing seam on the disclosed register-shift content argument (rejected_alternative citing 30:32's shift to second-person) rather than on tier-3 support that is not there.

items.claim: The admonition's threefold מִיץ repetition is byte-precise at verse-token positions 2/6/10 of 30:33, the closing petuchah at 30:33 correctly carries the C6|C7 collection seam (30:33|31:1), and the row transparently discloses that the tier-3 parashah segment spanning 30:29-33 does not itself break at the row's own 31|32 opening seam, weighing that competing texture against the row instead of concealing it.
items.evidence: oshb:Prov.30.32-33 מִ֪יץ/וּֽמִיץ/וּמִ֥יץ occur at word positions 2, 6, 10 of 30:33 exactly as claimed (counted against source bytes: כי-1 מיץ-2 חלב-3 יוציא-4 חמאה-5 ומיץ-6 אף-7 יוציא-8 דם-9 ומיץ-10); pmarks_Prov.json confirms PE at Prov.30.33 (single-witness) and no mark between Prov.30.29 and Prov.30.33, matching the device_notes' disclosure of one 5-verse tier-3 segment (30:29-33) that is not broken at the content-argued 31|32 seam.
tier_citations: tier-1 (register shift + threefold repetition, oshb text, re-collated)

items.claim: The rejected_alternative's claim that "the same vocative frame govern[s]" all seven verses from 31:2 to 31:8 ("7 of 7") overstates the grammatical uniformity of the unit: three of those seven verses depart from the second-person Lemuel address the row names as the governing frame.
items.evidence: oshb:Prov.31.5 (יִ֭שְׁתֶּה/וְיִשְׁכַּ֣ח/וִֽ֝ישַׁנֶּה) and oshb:Prov.31.7 (יִ֭שְׁתֶּה/וְיִשְׁכַּ֣ח) use third-person-masculine-singular verbs describing a third party, not second-person address to Lemuel, and oshb:Prov.31.6 (תְּנוּ) is a second-person-masculine-plural imperative to a different addressee/number than the second-person-masculine-singular frame at oshb:Prov.31.3 (תִּתֵּ֣ן) and oshb:Prov.31.8-9 (פְּתַח). Three of the seven verses the row counts as one continuous vocative frame are grammatically outside that frame; the row's own digit ('7 of 7') is not qualified against this texture. This does not disturb the owner-ruled single royal_instruction unit for 31:1-9 (the acrostic-adjacent seams at 30:33|31:1 and 31:9|31:10 are both independently well warranted by the disclosed petuchot), but the specific rebuttal offered against the 31:3-7/31:8-9 split rival is weaker than the '7 of 7' framing implies.
tier_citations: tier-1 (grammatical person, oshb text, re-derived verb-by-verb against source bytes)

items.claim: The acrostic_poem row correctly treats the book's own 22/22 alef-bet architecture as the sole governing boundary device, properly discloses the twice-occurring אֵֽשֶׁת חַ֭יִל opener (12:4 and 31:10) against any uniqueness claim, and correctly rests on the single bordering petuchah at 31:9 (the C7|C8 seam) with no interior tier-3 marks inside the span.
items.evidence: oshb:Prov.31.10 אֵֽשֶׁת חַ֭יִל byte-matches both here and at oshb:Prov.12.4 (identical bytes), confirming the sweep-digit-2 disclosure rather than a false 'unique' claim; the 22-letter first-word table in prov_device_inventory.json spot-checks correctly against verse_map_oshb.json (31:16 ז/זממה, 31:18 ט/טעמה, 31:20 כ/כפה, 31:22 מ/מרבדים all confirmed byte-true); pmarks_Prov.json shows no PE/SAMEKH inside Prov.31.10-Prov.31.31, only the bordering PE at Prov.31.9, and the K/Q at Prov.31.16/31.18 (inline ketiv נטע/בליל before the pointed qere) are correctly disclosed as routine density rather than interior-division evidence.
tier_citations: tier-1 (acrostic architecture + repeated phrase, oshb text, re-collated)
